notes: Sources inherited from the recommendation and first-government research retain their original access dates; newly retrieved sources were read on 2026-11-05.

The term window runs from this election to the next Knesset election. Government tenure may extend past that window. Mid-term institutional succession is recorded in formation.events; it is not a new post-election recommendation round.

Additional dated mid-term acts that do not fit the proposal’s closed formation type vocabulary are kept as formalStep=true entries in government.changes (Dated-compatible). No new formation enum values are introduced.

events.textEn: Ehud Barak was elected prime minister by direct vote; no presidential recommendation round was held.
events.textHe: אהוד ברק נבחר לראש הממשלה בבחירה ישירה; לא נערך סבב המלצות לנשיא.

cites.quote: Mr. Barak was elected Prime Minister
ראש הממשלה מכהן מכוח היבחרו בבחירות כלליות, ארציות, ישירות, שוות וחשאיות

events.textEn: The Knesset approved Barak’s 28th government and the ministers were sworn in.
events.textHe: הכנסת אישרה את הממשלה ה־28 בראשות ברק והשרים הושבעו.

cites.quote: the new Israeli government and policy guidelines were approved by the Knesset
par une majorité de 75 voix contre 29

events.textEn: Ariel Sharon was elected prime minister in a special PM-only election during the Fifteenth Knesset; no Knesset election or recommendation round was held.
events.textHe: אריאל שרון נבחר לראש הממשלה בבחירות מיוחדות לראשות הממשלה בלבד, במהלך כהונת הכנסת החמש־עשרה; לא נערכו בחירות לכנסת או סבב המלצות.

cites.quote: Ariel Sharon from the Likud on February 6, 2001
לבחור ראש ממשלה בלבד, בלי לבחור רשימה לכנסת

events.textEn: The Knesset approved Sharon’s 29th government, 72 for · 21 against.
events.textHe: הכנסת הביעה אמון בממשלה ה־29 בראשות שרון, 72 בעד · 21 נגד.

cites.quote: by a vote of 72-21, with 27 members absent
by a vote 72 to 21

term.inclusionRule: At least two independently authored qualifying chronologies, including one official or academic, plus direct support for the date. The Knesset and MFA histories count separately; the JVL mirror is not another independent source. Formal government succession steps are recorded separately in formation.events.

events.textEn: Israel withdrew its forces from southern Lebanon.
events.textHe: ישראל הסיגה את כוחותיה מדרום לבנון.

cites.quote: the IDF unilaterally withdrew from Lebanon
In May of 2000 Israel withdrew all its forces

events.textEn: Ehud Barak, Yasser Arafat and Bill Clinton met at Camp David; the summit ended without an agreement.
events.textHe: אהוד ברק, יאסר ערפאת וביל קלינטון נפגשו בקמפ דייוויד; הפסגה הסתיימה ללא הסכם.

cites.quote: on the Palestinian front at Camp David
attended a summit at Camp David in July 2000
The summit ended without an agreement

events.textEn: The Second Intifada began in September 2000 and included suicide bombings and other terror attacks against Israelis.
events.textHe: האינתיפאדה השנייה החלה בספטמבר 2000 וכללה פיגועי התאבדות ופיגועי טרור נוספים נגד ישראלים.

cites.quote: and suicide bombings.
In September 2000, the Second Intifada broke out
In September 2000, the Palestinians initiated an Intifada

events.textEn: Riots broke out in Arab communities in Israel; police fire killed Arab citizens.
events.textHe: מהומות פרצו ביישובים ערביים בישראל; אזרחים ערבים נהרגו מירי המשטרה.

cites.quote: In October, riots broke out in the Israeli Arab sector
In October 2000
were killed by police gunfire

notes: No casualty figure is copied: the Knesset text calls all 13 victims Israeli Arabs, whereas IDI distinguishes twelve Israeli Arabs.

events.textEn: Ariel Sharon won a special direct election for prime minister; the Fifteenth Knesset remained in office.
events.textHe: אריאל שרון ניצח בבחירות מיוחדות ישירות לראש הממשלה; הכנסת החמש־עשרה המשיכה בכהונתה.

cites.quote: Ariel Sharon from the Likud on February 6, 2001
Ariel Sharon ( Likud ) elected prime minister
לבחור ראש ממשלה בלבד, בלי לבחור רשימה לכנסת

events.textEn: Israel launched Operation Defensive Shield in Judea and Samaria after the Passover terror attack in Netanya.
events.textHe: ישראל פתחה במבצע חומת מגן ביהודה ושומרון בעקבות הפיגוע בליל הסדר בנתניה.

cites.quote: Operation "Defensive Shield," (March 29 – May 10, 2002).
At the end of March 2002, Operation Defensive Shield was initiated.
Israel launches Operation Defensive Shield
major Palestinian cities, villages and refugee camps in the West Bank

notes: The MOD chronology identifies the Park Hotel bombing on 27 March as the main trigger and dates Operation Defensive Shield to 29 March–10 May 2002; the latter is an operation endpoint, not a peace agreement. The inherited UN yearbook gives inconsistent 28/29 March launch dates; the Israeli official chronology controls.
ציר הזמן של משרד הביטחון מציין את הפיגוע במלון פארק ב־27 במרס כגורם המרכזי למבצע ומתארך אותו ל־29 במרס עד 10 במאי 2002; זהו מועד סיום המבצע ולא הסכם שלום.

candidatesPending.label: Rehavam Ze’evi assassination
candidatesPending.why: Knesset history selects the assassination but misdates it to 23 October 2000; MFA selects it under 2001. Exact day requires a direct record before promotion.

candidatesPending.label: Barak resignation and calling the special election
candidatesPending.why: MFA history dates resignation to December 2000; the Knesset history selects the 2001 special election, already included. The bundled resignation/calling act still needs a second chronology and direct resignation record.

endedBy.textEn: Prime Minister Sharon dissolved the Knesset with President Katsav’s consent; the election followed on 28 January 2003.
endedBy.textHe: ראש הממשלה שרון פיזר את הכנסת בהסכמת הנשיא קצב; הבחירות נערכו ב־28 בינואר 2003.

cites.quote: בתאריך ל׳ בחשוון תשס״ג (5.11.2002)
cites.locator: pp.26–27, paragraph 1; Sharon, with presidential consent, ordered dissolution under section 22.

issuePolling.gap: INES instrument exists; no qualifying published topline verified for this election. No microdata analysis performed.

gaps: The retained results notice was signed and published on 25 May 1999 (YP 4757); retained Knesset OData opening membership starts 7 June 1999. An independently earlier certification act and first-sitting protocol have not been retrieved.
Formation timeline is a sourced subset; missing steps must not be inferred from statutory maximum periods.

First-government coalition membership is reused from the existing first-government scheme, whose party membership evidence includes labelled Hebrew Wikipedia; a complete independent primary coalition agreement cross-check remains pending.

Knesset history mirror misdates Ze’evi’s assassination; the inaccurate date remains excluded. Government 29 faction membership and intermediate Barak-to-Sharon formal acts remain incomplete; membership snapshots alone do not establish the legal effective time of resignation.
Government 28 tenure independently checked against retained official gov28.pdf p.120: 6 July 1999–7 March 2001. Intermediate formal resignation/caretaker acts remain incomplete.

The UPI photo caption indexes a 75–29 confidence vote, but the original returned 403. The tally is held out until an inspectable original is obtained; coalition size 75 is independently verified by JTA.
